slides.question: Is 209 enough to win India the series?

concept: A mid-match setup post built on contrast. The hero greys out the two biggest names' scores (Rohit 7, Kohli 5) and puts the number that matters in bright white: 209 to defend for the series. Slide 2 is a bar chart of India's scorecard, so you can see at a glance that the innings leaned on two 46s from Axar and Kishan while the top three made 30 between them. Slide 3 explains the collapse (34/3 inside nine overs) and hands the question to fans while the chase is still live. Cricket blue tag, type and data only: no player photos, no board or team logos.
caption:
Rohit 7. Kohli 5. India 209 all out.

That's all India have to defend in the series decider at Bay Oval. New Zealand won their first toss of the tour, chose to bowl, and had India 34/3 inside nine overs: Matthew Fisher removed Rohit and Kohli, Jacob Duffy got Gaikwad.

Axar Patel and Ishan Kishan made 46 each. No Indian reached fifty. Mitchell Santner (3/47) and Duffy (3/60) finished the job in 42.1 overs.

India lead the series 2-1. Defend 210 and it's 3-1. Lose and New Zealand share it 2-2.

Is 209 enough? Tell us below.
